subject: Materials Science
title: The Galvanic Series
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Galvanic Series.

hook.text: Connect copper pipe to a steel radiator and the steel corrodes fast — the copper stays perfect.

buildup.text: The galvanic series ranks metals by their tendency to corrode in seawater — most active to most noble.

discovery.text: When two different metals touch in an electrolyte, the more active one corrodes to protect the nobler one.

twist.text: The further apart two metals are in the series, the faster the active one corrodes — distance matters.

climax.text: Marine engineers choose metals close together on the series — or insulate joints to prevent galvanic attack.

punchline.text: Pair the wrong metals and one sacrifices itself for the other.

quiz.question: What happens when two dissimilar metals touch in an electrolyte?
options: Both corrode at the same rate
The more active metal corrodes preferentially
